decisions.mark: explains that `skipSync: true` stops the single incoming reaction being treated as the post's complete set — without it every other reaction on the post would be deleted
decisions.detail: QUOTE: This is the single-reaction, event-driven case, so it must not treat the rest of the post's reactions as stale. | WHY: The answer says skipSync makes sanitizeReactions skip computing deleteReactions, so the lone incoming reaction isn't treated as the post's full set and the other reactions aren't treated as stale (and deleted). || QUOTE: This is the single-reaction, event-driven case, so it must not treat the rest of the post's reactions as stale. | WHY: The answer says skipSync: true skips deleteReactions computation because the single incoming reaction must not cause the post's other reactions to be treated as stale (deleted). || QUOTE: This is the single-reaction, event-driven case, so it must not treat the rest of the post's reactions as stale. | WHY: The answer says skipSync: true returns before computing deleteReactions because a single incoming reaction must not cause the post's other reactions to be treated as stale (deleted).
